tagline: Across the Osage on US 60, through old oil money.
intro: Out of Ponca City, US 60 crosses the Arkansas River into Osage County, which is also the Osage Nation reservation, and goes 21 miles before it meets another state highway near Burbank. It runs east through the Osage Hills and expanses of tallgrass prairie to Pawhuska, then north and east again toward Bartlesville.

Oil boomed here in the 1910s and 1920s. Leases on Osage land went at auction under the Million Dollar Elm in Pawhuska, with Marland, Frank Phillips and William G. Skelly bidding in its shade, and the Osage, who had kept their mineral rights in common, drew the royalties.

moments.title: Burbank
moments.text: A farm town of about 200 until Marland struck oil northeast of it in May 1920, Burbank swelled to 3,000 and was back down to 372 by 1930.

moments.title: Pawhuska
moments.text: The Osage government has kept its offices here since 1872, and the Osage Nation Museum, founded in 1938, is the oldest tribally owned museum in the country.

moments.title: Osage Hills State Park
moments.text: One of Oklahoma's seven original parks, built by the CCC from 1935 in local stone and timber, where a lone chimney still marks the workers' camp.
